    <div>
      <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><strong>14.</strong><span style="width:5.49pt;text-indent:0pt;display:inline-block">&#160;</span><strong>Term Loan </strong></span></span></p>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">As part of the Atlantic acquisition, the Company acquired an $<ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250618050427359" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_20210331_usgaapDebtInstrumentAxis_hiveAtlanticTermLoansMember" unitRef="USD" scale="6" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">11.0</ix:nonFraction> million (C$<ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250618050433390" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_20210331_usgaapDebtInstrumentAxis_hiveAtlanticTermLoansMember" unitRef="CAD" scale="6" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">13.6</ix:nonFraction> million) term loan ("Atlantic Term Loans"). The Atlantic Term Loans were made up of two discrete balances; Term Loan 1 and Term Loan 2; and the total facility bearing an interest rate of <ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250618050500847" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_20210331_usgaapDebtInstrumentAxis_hiveAtlanticTermLoansMember" unitRef="Pure" scale="-2" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">3.33</ix:nonFraction>% per annum with a term maturity date of June 30, 2024.</span></span></p>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">On June 30, 2024, the Company renewed Term Loan 1 over a 1-year term at an interest rate of <ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250618050646711" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_20240630_usgaapDebtInstrumentAxis_hiveAtlanticTermLoansMember_usgaapShortTermDebtTypeAxis_hiveTermLoanOneMember" unitRef="Pure" scale="-2" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">5.31</ix:nonFraction>% with a balance remaining of C$<ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250618050744050" name="us-gaap:ShortTermBorrowings" contextRef="C_20240630_usgaapDebtInstrumentAxis_hiveAtlanticTermLoansMember_usgaapShortTermDebtTypeAxis_hiveTermLoanOneMember" unitRef="CAD" scale="6" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">4.2</ix:nonFraction> million, and Term Loan 2 was renewed at <ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250618050651488" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_20240630_usgaapDebtInstrumentAxis_hiveAtlanticTermLoansMember_usgaapShortTermDebtTypeAxis_hiveTermLoanTwoMember" unitRef="Pure" scale="-2" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">5.15</ix:nonFraction>% over a 2-year term with a balance remaining of C$<ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250618050736854" name="us-gaap:ShortTermBorrowings" contextRef="C_20240630_usgaapDebtInstrumentAxis_hiveAtlanticTermLoansMember_usgaapShortTermDebtTypeAxis_hiveTermLoanTwoMember" unitRef="CAD" scale="6" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">2.6</ix:nonFraction> million. Principal payments of C$<ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250618050741136" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentPeriodicPayment" contextRef="C_20240601to20240630_usgaapDebtInstrumentAxis_hiveAtlanticTermLoansMember" unitRef="CAD" scale="6" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.2</ix:nonFraction> million plus interest is payable monthly.</span></span></p>
      <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">On June 30, 2025, the Company renewed Term Loan 1 over a 1-year term at an interest rate of <ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250810181907064" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_20250630_usgaapDebtInstrumentAxis_hiveAtlanticTermLoansMember_usgaapShortTermDebtTypeAxis_hiveTermLoanOneMember" unitRef="Pure" scale="-2" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">4.39</ix:nonFraction>% with a balance&#160;remaining of C$<ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250810181926156" name="us-gaap:ShortTermBorrowings" contextRef="C_20250630_usgaapDebtInstrumentAxis_hiveAtlanticTermLoansMember_usgaapShortTermDebtTypeAxis_hiveTermLoanOneMember" unitRef="CAD" scale="6" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">2.8</ix:nonFraction> million. The principal and interest payment are the same as noted above.</span></span></p>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">On April 21, 2025, the Company received a covenant amendment from its lender in relation to the Atlantic Term Loans maintained by HIVE Atlantic Datacentres Ltd. As part of this modification, the lender formally withdrew the following financial covenants:</span></span></p>
      <ul style="padding-left:0pt;list-style-type:disc">
        <li style="margin-left:27.14pt;text-align:justify;padding-left:8.86pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">A minimum working capital ratio of 1.20:1</span></span></li>
        <li style="margin-left:27.14pt;text-align:justify;padding-left:8.86pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">A maximum long-term debt to tangible net worth ratio of 2.00:1</span></span></li>
      </ul>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">The following covenant remains in effect and must be maintained at all times:</span></span></p>
      <ul style="padding-left:0pt;list-style-type:disc">
        <li style="margin-left:27.14pt;text-align:justify;padding-left:8.86pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">A minimum debt service coverage ratio to EBITDA of 1.50:1</span></span></li>
      </ul>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">As at March 31, 2026, HIVE Atlantic Datacentres Ltd. was in compliance with the amended required debt service coverage ratio covenant. The outstanding balance is presented as a current liability as at March 31, 2026, because it matures within one year. The Atlantic Term Loans include an unlimited guarantee from the Company.</span></span></p>

        <div>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><strong>17.&#160; </strong><strong>Commitments and Contingencies</strong></span></span></p>
          <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><i>Commitments </i></span></span></p>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">(a)&#160; &#160;Service agreements</span></span></p>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">The Company has service agreements with unrelated third parties to operate and maintain the Company's data center computing equipment for the purpose of mining crypto currency in Canada, Sweden and Iceland.&#160; As part of the arrangement, proprietary software is installed on the Company's computing equipment to assist in optimizing the use of the equipment.</span></span></p>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">(b)&#160; &#160;Power purchase agreement</span></span></p>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">The Company entered into a supplemental power pricing arrangement that provides a fixed price of electricity consumption each month at the Company's Bikupa Datacenter AB and Bikupa Datacenter 2 AB location in Sweden. The fixed price agreement was assessed and is being accounted for as an executory contract; electricity costs are expensed as incurred.</span></span></p>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">(c)&#160; &#160;Obligations on mining equipment and development costs</span></span></p>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">The Company had purchase commitments of $<ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250617195020056" name="us-gaap:PurchaseObligation" contextRef="C_20260331" unitRef="USD" scale="6" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">29.1</ix:nonFraction> million at the year ended March 31, 2026 (March 31, 2025 - $<ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250617195112048" name="us-gaap:PurchaseObligation" contextRef="C_20250331" unitRef="USD" scale="6" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">227.8</ix:nonFraction> million).</span></span></p>
          <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><i>Contingencies</i></span></span></p>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">(a)&#160; &#160;Contingent VAT Liability to the Sweden Tax Agency ("STA")</span></span></p>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">The Company's wholly owned subsidiaries located in Sweden (Bikupa Datacenter AB ("Bikupa") and Bikupa Datacenter 2 AB ("Bikupa 2")) received decision notice of assessments ("the decision(s)"), on December 28, 2022, December 21, 2023, December 22, 2023, May 28, 2024, October 14 and 16, 2024, March 18, 2025, September 23, 2025, October 14, 2025 for Bikupa and February 14, 2023, December 21, 2023, June 14, 2024, September 11 and 23, 2024, March 21, 2025, June 12, 2025, August 11, 2025, November 26, 2025 and March 25, 2026 for Bikupa 2 respectively, from the Swedish Tax Agency in connection with the application of VAT and its ability to recover input VAT against certain equipment and other charges in a total amount of SEK <ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250617195202672" name="hive:InputTaxRecoveryObligations" contextRef="C_20250401to20260331" unitRef="SEK" scale="6" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">765.6</ix:nonFraction> million or approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="Fxbrl_20250617195237336" name="hive:InputTaxRecoveryObligations" contextRef="C_20250401to20260331" unitRef="USD" scale="6" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">80.5</ix:nonFraction> million. The assessments cover the period December 2020 to June 2025 for Bikupa, and the period April 2021 to December 2025 for Bikupa 2, expressing the intent to reject the recovery of all the VAT for the periods under assessment and repayment of amounts previously received plus applicable interest.</span></span></p>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">The Company filed a formal appeal in connection with the December 28, 2022, Bikupa decision on February 9, 2023; however, there can be no guarantee that the Company will achieve a favourable outcome in its appeal. A formal appeal for Bikupa 2 in relation to the February 14, 2023, decision was filed on March 10, 2023, by the Company. The Company engaged an independent legal firm and independent audit firm in Sweden with expertise in these matters to assist in the appeal process. The Company does not believe that the decision has merit because in management's opinion and those of the Company's independent advisors, the decision is not compatible with the current applicable law and therefore the amount claimed to be owed by the Company is not probable.&#160; According to general principles regarding the placement of the burden of proof, it is up to the Swedish Tax Agency to provide sufficient evidence in support of its decision. It is the Company's opinion; the Swedish Tax Agency has not substantiated their claim. We are not aware of any precedent cases, authoritative literature, or other statement that supports the STA's position. EU guidelines and a ruling from the Swedish Council for Advance Tax Rulings together with an IT forensic expert opinion and legal opinion from a Swedish Professor of VAT support the company&#8217;s position. The cases have gone through the Administrative Court and the Court of Appeal and are currently being appealed by the company to the Supreme Administrative Court.</span></span></p>
          <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">It is not yet known when this dispute will be resolved; the due process following appeals and the court ruling could extend beyond a year. Furthermore, given that the industry is rapidly developing, there can be no guarantee that changes to the laws or policies of Sweden will not have a negative impact on the Company's tax position with respect to the eligibility of the claimed VAT.</span></span></p>

        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><strong>Uncertain tax positions </strong></span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">Various foreign jurisdictions have, and may continue to adopt laws, regulations or directives that affect a digital asset network, the digital asset markets, and their users, particularly digital asset exchanges and service providers that fall within such jurisdictions' regulatory scope.&#160; For example, if China or other foreign jurisdictions were to ban or continue to otherwise restrict mining activity, including by regulating or limiting manufacturers' ability to produce or sell semiconductors or hard drives in connection with mining, it would have a material adverse effect on digital asset networks, the digital asset market, and as a result, impact our business.</span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">A number of foreign jurisdictions have recently taken regulatory action aimed at digital asset activities.&#160; China has made transacting in digital currencies illegal for Chinese citizens in mainland China, and additional restrictions may follow.&#160; As recently as September 2021, China's central bank has further restricted digital asset-related activities, stating that activity by overseas digital asset exchanges, and services offering trading, order matching, and token issuance and derivatives, constitute illegal activity.&#160; Both China and South Korea have banned initial coin offerings entirely and regulators in other jurisdictions, including Canada, Singapore, and Hong Kong, have opined that initial coin offerings may constitute securities offerings subject to local securities regulations.&#160; In September 2021, the Chinese government announced issued a complete ban that restricts digital currencies trading and mining activities, citing concerns about high energy consumption and its desire to promote financial stability.&#160; Regulators in the Inner Mongolia and other&#160; regions of China have proposed regulations that would create penalties for companies engaged in digital currency mining activities and introduce heightened energy saving requirements on industrial parks, data centers and power plants providing electricity to digital currency miners.&#160; The effect of the China ban was a movement of those miners and their hashrates out of China and into other countries.&#160; The United Kingdom's Financial Conduct Authority published final rules in October 2020 banning the sale of derivatives and exchange traded notes that reference certain types of digital currencies, contending that they are "ill-suited" to retail investors citing extreme volatility, valuation challenges and association with financial crime.</span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">Foreign laws, regulations or directives may conflict with those of the jurisdiction we operate in and may negatively impact the acceptance of one or more digital assets by users, merchants and service providers and may therefore impede the growth or sustainability of the digital asset economy in the European Union, China, Japan, Russia and the</span></span></p>
        <div style="margin-top:1pt;clear:both">
          <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">United States and globally, or otherwise negatively affect the value of digital assets that we invest in.&#160; The effect of any future regulatory change on our business or the digital assets that we invest in is impossible to predict, but such change could be substantial and adverse to our investment and trading strategies, the value of our assets and our investment value.</span></span></p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">(a)<span style="width:7pt;text-indent:0pt;display:inline-block">&#160;</span>Stock options</span></span></p>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">The Company has established a rolling Stock Option Plan (the "Plan"). Under the Plan, the number of shares reserved for issuance may not exceed 10% of the total number of issued and outstanding shares and, to any one optionee, may not exceed 5% of the issued shares on a yearly basis. The maximum term of each option shall not be greater than <ix:nonNumeric id="Fxbrl_20250618191203095" name="hive:StockOptionPlanMaximumTerm" contextRef="C_20250401to20260331_usgaapPlanNameAxis_hiveStockOptionPlanMember" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years. The exercise price of each option shall not be less than the market price of the Company's shares at the date of grant. Options granted to consultants performing investor relations activities shall vest over a minimum of 12 months with no more than a quarter of such options vesting in any 3-month period. All other options vest at the discretion of the Board of Directors. There were no options granted during the years ended March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025.</span></span></p>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">On April 1, 2024, the Company modified the exercise price from Canadian dollars to United States dollars of stock options that were held by employees in the United States of America and in Europe. The modification resulted in $nil additional stock-based compensation expense.&#160;</span></span></p>

      <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">(b)<span style="width:7pt;text-indent:0pt;display:inline-block">&#160;</span>Restricted share-units</span></span></p>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">The Company has established a Restricted Share Unit Plan (the "RSU Plan"). Under the RSU Plan, together with any other share compensation arrangement, the number of shares reserved for issuance may not exceed 10% of the total number of issued and outstanding shares and, to any one optionee, may not exceed 5% of the issued shares on a yearly basis. The Board may in its own discretion, at any time, and from time to time, grant RSUs to any employee, director or consultant of the Company or its subsidiaries (collectively, "Eligible Person"), other than persons conducting investor relations activities, from time to time by the Board, subject to the limitations set forth in the RSU Plan. The Board may designate one or more performance periods under the RSU Plan.&#160; In respect of each designated performance period and subject to the terms of the RSU Plan, the Board may from time to time establish the grant date and grant to any Eligible Person one or more RSUs as the Board deems appropriate.</span></span></p>

  <ix:nonNumeric id="Fxbrl_20260512135757915" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" contextRef="C_20250401to20260331" escape="true">
    <div>
      <div>
        <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span><span><strong>27.</strong><span style="width:5.49pt;text-indent:0pt;display:inline-block">&#160;</span><strong>Fair Value Measurements</strong></span></span></span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span><span>The fair values of investments were measured using the NAV or a market approach. The investments measured at fair value are classified into one of the three levels in the fair value hierarchy according to the relative reliability of the inputs used to estimate the fair values, with the designation based upon the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement.&#160; The three levels of the fair value hierarchy are:</span></span></span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span><span><i>Level 1 Inputs:</i> Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the entity can access at the measurement date.</span></span></span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span><span><i>Level 2 Inputs:</i> Quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, or quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are not active, or other observable inputs other than quoted prices. At March 31, 2026 the Company reclassified digital currencies from Level 2 fair value measurement to Level 1 to reflect the market prices available for digital assets. The comparatives have been reclassified to conform with the current presentation.</span></span></span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span><span><i>Level 3 Inputs:</i> Unobservable inputs for the asset or liability (Unobservable inputs reflect management's assumptions on how market participants would price the asset or liability based on the information available).</span></span></span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span><span><i>Valuation of Assets that use Level 2 Inputs ("Level 2 Assets")</i>.&#160; The fair value of Level 2 Assets would use the quoted price from the exchanges which the Company most frequently uses, with no adjustment.</span></span></span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span><span>At the year end the Company classified its financial assets into the following levels:</span></span></span></span></p>

        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span><span>A verified prior transaction is initially given 100% weighting in a fair value conclusion (if completed at arm's length), but subsequently such weighting is adjusted based on the merits of newly observed data.&#160; As a result, in the absence of disconfirming data, an unadjusted prior transaction price may not be considered "stale" for months or, in some cases, years.</span></span></span></span></p>

              <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span><span>In addition to assets and liabilities that are measured at fair value on a recurring basis, the Company also measures certain assets and liabilities at fair value on a non-recurring basis. The Company&#8217;s long-lived assets, including intangible assets, operating lease right-of-use assets, and property, plant and equipment, are measured at fair value when there is an indication of impairment and the carrying amount exceeds the asset&#8217;s projected undiscounted cash flows.</span></span></span></span></p>
              <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span><span>These assets are measured at fair value only when an impairment loss is recognized. The carrying amounts of cash, amounts receivable, net, other receivables, and accounts payable and accrued expenses are a reasonable approximation of their fair value due to their short-term maturity or they are valued using the income approach valuation technique.</span></span></span></span></p>

      <p style="margin-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><strong>28.</strong><span style="width:5.49pt;text-indent:0pt;display:inline-block">&#160;</span><strong>Digital Currency and Risk Management </strong></span></span></p>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">Digital currencies are measured using Level 1 inputs</span></span></p>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">Digital currency prices are affected by various forces including global supply and demand, interest rates, exchange rates, inflation or deflation and the global political and economic conditions.&#160; The profitability of the Company is directly related to the current and future market price of coins; in addition, the Company may not be able liquidate its inventory of digital currency at its desired price if required.&#160; A decline in the market prices for coins could negatively impact the Company's future operations.&#160; The Company has not hedged the conversion of any of its coin sales or future mining of digital currencies.&#160;</span></span></p>
      <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">Digital currencies have a limited history and the fair value historically has been very volatile.&#160; Historical performance of digital currencies is not indicative of their future price performance.&#160; The Company's digital currencies currently mainly consist of Bitcoin.&#160; The table below shows the impact for every 5% variance in the price of Bitcoin on the Company's earnings before tax, based on the closing price at March 31, 2026.</span></span></p>

        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span id="page_91"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><strong>Item 9. </strong></span></span></span><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><strong>Changes In And Disagreements With Accountants On Accounting And Financial Disclosure</strong></span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">None</span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><strong>Item 9.A Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</strong></span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">Our Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining a system of disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)) designed to ensure that information we are required to disclose in the reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms. Disclosure controls and procedures include, without limitation, controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in our reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">Management, under the supervision of and with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, has evaluated the design and effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures as of March 31, 2026. Based upon such evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that, as of March 31, 2026, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective.</span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">A control system, no matter how well conceived and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that its objectives are met. Due to inherent limitations in all such systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues within a company have been detected. Accordingly, our disclosure controls and procedures are designed to provide reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of our disclosure control system are met.</span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><strong>Management's Annual Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting:</strong></span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (&#8220;ICFR&#8221;) for the Company as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act. Our internal control system is designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;U.S. GAAP&#8221;). All internal control systems, no matter how well designed, have inherent limitations. Therefore, even those systems determined to be effective can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance with respect to financial statement preparation and presentation.</span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">Management, under the supervision of and with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of March 31, 2026 &#160;based on the criteria set forth in Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (&#8220;COSO&#8221;). Based on this assessment, management has concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of March 31, 2026.</span></span></p>
        <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif">The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of March 31, 2026, has been audited by Davidson &amp; Company LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in their report which appears in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</span></span></p>
